terms.gloss: a rule, a standard to judge by
evidence: Cic. Brut. 152: rēgula, quā vēra et falsa jūdicārentur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.110: nostrae nātūrae rēgulā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally a ruler, the carpenter’s straight-edge; figuratively the rule by which a thing is measured or judged (Lewis & Short). It is also a rule of conduct (see rule).

evidence: Cic. Mur. 3: vītam ad certam ratiōnis normam dīrigere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally a carpenter’s square; figuratively a rule or pattern, especially of conduct (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nōs studia nostra nostrae nātūrae rēgulā mētiāmur
phrases.english: let us measure our pursuits by the standard of our own nature

phrases.latin: rēgula, quā vēra et falsa jūdicārentur
phrases.english: a rule by which true and false could be judged

sources: Lewis & Short: regula · Lewis & Short: norma
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
